title: The ADHD Wall of Awful: Why You Can't Start What You Love #Shorts
description:
The wall of awful is real neuroscience — your brain's limbic system stores every past emotional failure and fires the whole archive before you even open the file. Learn why the things you care about are hardest to start and the one low-stakes proximity trick that quietly lowers the wall. Free 2-minute ADHD brain quiz: https://bloomfocus.org/quiz
Follow for daily ADHD content.

voiceover: You walk into the kitchen with a clear mission. By the time you get there, it's gone. That's not forgetfulness — that's your working memory dropping the thought the second something new entered your field of view. ADHD brains have lower dopamine availability in the prefrontal cortex, which is the region that holds information 'online' while you act on it. No dopamine signal, no active hold — the thought simply ceases to exist. The fix isn't writing everything down after it vanishes. It's externalising the thought before you move. Say it out loud. One word, out loud, the second it arrives: 'kettle', 'email', 'keys'. Your voice becomes the external hard drive your prefrontal cortex can't be right now. The thought lives in the air, not in a brain that was never built to hold it quietly. Follow for daily ADHD content.
